label: Late in the episode, D1 update gate drops sharply after reaching S2, less if rewarded.
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/4) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/4) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/4) ;; (phase == D1) * (tv("state", -2) == 2) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/4) ;; (phase == D1) * belief_lo * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/4) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 u") ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 r") ;; (phase == GO) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/4) * (prev_state==2)
explanation: Raw z of unit 42 sits near 1 almost always; its variance is a D1 dip in the last ~10 trials of the episode (timing baseline). Beyond timing, the dip is much deeper when the previous trial reached S2 (the S2-state effect grows roughly exponentially toward trial 99), and somewhat smaller when the previous trial was rewarded; throughout the episode there is also a small constant D1 drop after an a1->S2 (rare) trial. GO and D2 barely vary. Belief, the choice being made and hidden/future variables add little. The free fit adds a few points with the state two trials back (fitted weight positive: S2 two trials back slightly offsets the dip late), belief_lo and a GO-phase late S2 term. Observed-only; the profile additive ceiling (0.17) is below this because it lacks the lateness interaction.

issues: Main claims hold on test. Short form 0.417. The late-S2 term alone gives 0.306. Adding the late-reward term gives 0.363 (weight +0.10, so a reward does make the dip smaller). The free fit gives 0.456, and a wider 8-term fit tops out at about 0.478, so the short form gets most of what is available.

The explanation says the a1->S2 (rare) drop is a 'small fixed D1 drop throughout the episode'. That is misleading. Splitting the term by trial gives weight -0.021 before trial 80 and -0.080 from trial 80 on (test 0.453). With a late a1->S2 interaction, that term's weight is -0.195 and the fixed part falls to -0.026 (0.462). So late in the episode the dip after rare a1->S2 is deeper (about -0.47) than after common a2->S2 (about -0.27). The rare effect is mostly a lateness effect, not a constant one.
The label leaves out the rare-transition part, even though the short form has a term for it. Dropping that term costs 0.055 test R^2 (0.417 to 0.363).

An alternative short form, (D1)*(prev_state==2)*E ;; (D1)*(prev_state>prev_action)*E ;; (D1)*(prev_reward==1)*E, scores 0.431 on test. But misses shows it over-predicts the dip by about -0.02 after a1 S2 r and a1 S2 u. The recorded form has no systematic error larger than about 0.012 (under-predicted D1 after S1 trials), so I kept the recorded form.

Misses on the recorded form: the mean error by phase is at most 0.004. The worst windows are single very deep D1 dips (about 0.35-0.40) around trials 94-97 that the exponential shape under-predicts. These look like spread in how deep the dip goes, not a pattern in the previous trial. Time constants 3 and 6 score 0.410 and 0.411 against 0.417 for 4, so the choice of 4 is not tuned to a sharp optimum.
Belief adds little in short forms: swapping belief_lo*lateness in for the reward term gives 0.389 versus 0.417, so the claim that belief adds little holds. No future variables are used.
skeptic.revised_label: Late-episode D1 update gate dips after reaching S2, deeper after rare a1->S2, shallower if rewarded.
